comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Janitor run 2026-08-05/06 complete through Phase 5. Discovery fanned out across 9 concerns (incl. user-added sweeps: unwired/partially-wired functionality, comment quality, and a 4-shard test-suite audit); 73 candidates went to blind verification, 27 cleared validity>=0.75 and impact>=0.5. Two fabricated citations produced by the audit's own discovery agents were caught by the verification pass. Remediation used two blind proposers: 16/20 moves converged; 4 divergent items went to OSS research, which overturned both proposers twice. Audit record: .joe-janitor/report-2026-08-06.md.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Decisions that a future run should not re-derive. (a) Per-ticket last-synced timestamp REJECTED on measured evidence: it is mechanically a revert of ADR 0060 section A1, whose 12.79KB->1.74KB measurement was taken on that exact field; ~69 of 72 daily passes currently produce zero bridge-state commits because every writer is change-guarded, and an always-written timestamp inverts that (~180x churn). updated_at cannot stand in for 'last synced' - 908 of 1914 entries are byte-identical to created_at. (b) 'bridge status' needs no new producer: last-run time is derivable three independent ways that agree; only the health record needs redirecting to a durable path. (c) The pause mechanism is inverted today - the portable, remote-persisted ref-lock gate has no writer while the GitHub-specific 'gh workflow disable' is the wired path, which is the portability violation driving the bridge epic. (d) 'jira' rejected as the noun (other trackers planned); 'bridge' approved; 'reconcile' retired without an alias. (e) The 800-LOC cap acts as an attractor - 11 of 24 cap-crowding files fall into the 200-500 target band once comments are triaged, but event_append.py, _processors.py and signing.py cannot be fixed that way (replay-compat and security invariants).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Final spike (bridge fsck phantom checks) landed after the other deliverables; filed as ninth bridge child 030f-c14f-596a-4f79. Key result: three of bridge fsck's four advertised checks are permanently empty because SYNC events NEVER existed in rebar - the module was ported verbatim from the pre-rebar digital-service-orchestra plugin (extraction commit b534f47a7f) and 'if not sync_events: continue' short-circuits every ticket dir. On origin/tickets today: 39216 event files, 0 SYNC, 0 BRIDGE_ALERT. The fourth advertised check (unresolved BRIDGE_ALERT counts) was never backed by code in any commit. This independently re-derived janitor ticket 8efe (BridgeFsckOut omits binding_drift) from a different starting point. Two real gaps remain: count_unresolved_alerts is implemented but gated behind .bridge-status.json, a file with no producer anywhere in the tree or history; and bindings.json's reverse map is read but never validated for forward/reverse consistency, which would be the one bridge audit decidable fully offline with zero Jira access. Five decisions recorded on the ticket, incl. whether the never-fired BRIDGE_ALERT emitter should survive at all.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: ARG decision (item 17): sweep approved, gate deliberately NOT enabled. Filed story fc0c-e218-8b34-4858 (43 mechanical fixes + two cluster decisions) and bug c9c6-a713-8bc6-4088 (update_priority accepts acli_cmd it cannot use). Deciding evidence: _-prefixing is not a safe universal remediation here - typed_dispatch.py:128 reads parameter names as strings and client is passed unconditionally, so renames break dispatch at runtime; and a gate would require ~17 permanent inline noqa, a discretionary per-site hatch this project has ruled against. OSS survey found zero ARG reversions across ~15 repos, but the exclusion is near-universal and always same-commit-as-adoption, so it is 'predicted the cost' not 'recanted'. Nobody documented ARG catching a real bug; rebar caught three. Revisit note recorded in .joe-janitor/tools.md keyed to the irreducible exception count the sweep will measure.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Janitor skill validation redesign - decisions so far (pending two research reports). APPROVED: (1) intent check folded into the FIRST validation pass, triggered subject-scoped rather than verb-scoped - item 16 proposed an ADDITION ('persist the close reason') that was a reversal only at the subject level, so a removal-verb trigger would have missed it; queries are git log -S, the originating commit's rebar-ticket trailer, ADR grep, and comments citing ticket ids. (2) Proposer decorrelation by QUESTION, not just reading list: Proposer A gets web search and answers 'how does the community do this', Proposer B answers 'how does this project do this' from the record; both grounded in the code. This covers the remediation-property error class - '_-prefixing is safe' was refuted by ruff#10409, which Proposer A would have surfaced at proposal time. (3) 'Is the harm reachable' sub-question, requiring a concrete triggering input/state; un-demonstrable is classified HARDENING not DEFECT (would have downgraded the B905 claim). REJECTED: a basis/confidence-provenance field. DECIDED: no second validation pass and no validation at synthesis - the synthesizer is the orchestrator and therefore the invested party, which is the failure mode observed this run. (4) Divergence between proposers drives an additional targeted research round asking WHY, specifically whether the community has EXPLICITLY REJECTED the project's approach; divergence remains a finding reported with both positions and their evidence, never a synthesized winner.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Janitor validation redesign - correction to the intent check. The intent check must NOT veto. A prior project decision is an N of 1 and may be reversed with good cause; treating 'the record says this was deliberate' as blocking would make the janitor structurally unable to recommend undoing a decision that aged badly, which is most of its purpose. Revised: the check produces a prior_decision record the proposal must ENGAGE, not obey. A reversal is legitimate when it names (a) the decision, (b) what evidence has changed since, (c) why the original reasoning no longer holds. Missing (b) is an UNINFORMED reversal and is what gets flagged. Tested against both observed failures: item 16 (persist close reason) fails on (b) - ed13 was recent and nothing had changed, correct block. Item 19 permits the outcome actually reached - wiring SupportsIncremental for both Jira providers DID supersede ce4d's negative-fixture framing, with cause, so the same mechanism blocks the uninformed reversal and permits the informed one. Corollary for divergence: neither record is authoritative. Project record = high context-fit, low statistical weight, may be stale. Community record = high statistical weight, low context-fit, may be cargo-culted - the ARG survey's dominant 'excluded at adoption' bucket is precisely a population that never tested its own prediction.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Cross-model context (research launched; NO janitor revisions from it - context only, per maintainer). Motivation: the OSS-practice survey found cross-model critique is the one decorrelation mechanism with clean empirical support - Greptile's Model Inversion measured a model reviewing same-model-authored code at 53.7% recall vs 62.0% on another model's code, because 'the types of bugs a model introduces most often are the same types it's more likely to miss during review'; Goel et al. arXiv:2502.04313 report mistakes growing MORE similar as capability rises, and that LLM-judge scores favour models similar to the judge. Our current config is single-family: DEFAULT_MODEL claude-opus-4-8 (frontier), VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL claude-sonnet-4-6 (standard), DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6. Provider is inferred from the model name through pydantic-ai, so a non-Anthropic provider is already architecturally supported - this would be configuration, not new plumbing. Hard constraints on any candidate: Bedrock inference-profile id (plain on-demand ids raise ValidationException), and RELIABLE schema-constrained structured output, since every rebar LLM operation forces JSON-Schema output through pydantic-ai. Key framing recorded for whoever revisits: the goal is decorrelation, not replacement, so a slightly weaker model that fails DIFFERENTLY can be worth more as a reviewer than a stronger model that fails the same way.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Two Phase-4 REJECTIONS, recorded so a future janitor run does not re-raise them. (1) The gerrit-verify.yaml concurrency guard (lines 40-43): group keyed on GERRIT_CHANGE_ID with cancel-in-progress:true, so any re-dispatch for a change cancels its queued predecessor and a cancelled run posts Verified -1. Observed live during a ~2h GitHub hosted-runner outage on change 1452, which then merged on a human-cast Verified +1 with no CI run. REJECTED by the maintainer - do not re-file. (2) A separate validation gate on remediation proposals - i.e. scoring 'is the observation true' independently from 'is the recommendation right'. The OSS-practice survey found no system does this and called the split 'genuinely novel' for a recommendations pipeline, but the janitor's own coverage analysis showed all four observed error classes are already handled upstream by the subject-scoped intent check, the harm-reachability sub-question, and the community-vs-project proposer decorrelation. Building a pass for an unobserved failure mode is the speculative structure the skill's own concern #8 warns against. REJECTED - do not re-raise without an observed instance.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: 2026 error-detection research returned. KEY FINDINGS vs our design. (1) CONFIRMS the diagnosis with a 2023 citation: RARR (Gao et al., ACL 2023) documented this exact bug - 'RARR currently does not try to modify subsequent reasoning steps which may no longer be logically entailed', plus footnote 'attribution does not entail correctness'. Our citation veto is an ATTRIBUTION gate; attribution gates provably do not catch invalid inference. (2) CONTRADICTS a fixed design decision: the Phase-3 convergence rule (same_approach OR same_end_state) is actively contraindicated by tier-(a) replicated evidence - Huang et al. show debate underperforms self-consistency at matched compute; the 2026 conformity wave measures 85.5% modal adoption, 70% vulnerability, and 57-77% of conformity being correct-to-wrong; Pan et al. name the 'consensus trap'; Wang and Yang show answer-level consensus does not entail reasoning-level alignment. Agreement between proposers is close to no evidence under shared priors. (3) NEW, cheapest high-value change - PRE-COMMITMENT/de-anchoring: Zhou arXiv:2607.05904 finds 'conditioned on a candidate, a judge scores plausibility, not correctness' and that committing an answer first drops judge false-positive rate 0.719 to 0.012. We have blindness but NOT pre-commitment. (4) QUALIFIES the approved intent check: 'retrieved the right record' and 'acted on it' are separately-failing capabilities - STALE 55.2%, MemoryAgentBench <=28% multi-hop even when handed the ordering rule. The hardest case, triangulated across three unrelated literatures, is IMPLICIT conflict where a later decision invalidates an earlier one without explicit negation - which is exactly the item-16 shape (ed13 replaced free-text with a bounded class rather than negating anything). Implication: the intent check must SURFACE the record, not adjudicate it. (5) SUPPORTS the basis-field rejection: knowing-saying gap - internal representations discriminate correctness at 0.92-0.99 AUROC while verbalized confidence sits at 0.50-0.63; Advani finds TF-IDF detectors beat LLM judges at spotting agent overclaiming (0.83/0.95 vs 0.65/0.54). Caveat: the specific executed/read/inferred variant is UNTESTED rather than disproven.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: CORRECTIONS to two claims I propagated this session, both caught by verifying primary sources. (1) The Greptile Model Inversion numbers were misstated by me, twice, including inside a brief I sent to a research agent. I reported "Claude reviewing Claude-authored code 53.7% vs Claude reviewing GPT-authored 62.0%", an 8.3pt gap. Verified table: Claude Opus 4.7 scores 60.0% on Claude-authored PRs (self) and 53.7% on Codex-authored (cross); GPT-5.5 scores 62.0% on Claude-authored (cross) and 50.5% on Codex-authored (self). 53.7 and 62.0 are BOTH cross cells, from DIFFERENT datasets. Real self-vs-cross gaps are 2.0pt and 3.2pt. Direction supports the decorrelation thesis; magnitude is about a third of what I claimed. No significance testing, heuristic ground truth, and Greptile argued the opposite position in May 2025. (2) Goel et al. arXiv:2502.04313 cannot be cited for "Claude and GPT fail differently". Verified: similarity measurements cover OPEN-WEIGHT models only (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral); Claude and OpenAI models are absent; benchmarks are MMLU-Pro, BIG-Bench Hard and AlpacaEval with NO code tasks; and the paper deliberately excludes same-developer pairs to avoid distillation confounds. Both errors are the failure mode this run has been auditing: relaying a subagent framing without checking the source.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Janitor skill design - three further rulings. (2) CONVERGENCE RULE UNCHANGED. The maintainer's rebuttal: the cited consensus research studies agreement across IDENTICAL inputs (sycophancy, peer pressure, modal adoption), whereas our proposers are blind to each other AND hold different evidence bases. Agreement across decorrelated inputs is triangulation, not conformity, so the conformity literature does not transfer. Accepted. (3) PRE-COMMITMENT REJECTED as a different shape from our process. Zhou's finding targets a judge asked for a holistic "is this right?" verdict on a candidate. Our verification decomposes into narrow binary sub-questions plus the citation veto plus harm-reachability, which already moves scoring from general impression to specific measurable facets - the same mechanism reached by another route. Accepted. (4) INTENT CHECK now also feeds SCORING, not just reporting. Surface the record, require the proposal to address it, pass the intent information through to the user for review - and apply a scoring penalty when a deliberate prior decision exists and the proposal does not name what evidence has changed. Effect is that a MARGINAL finding is dropped while a strong one survives contact with the record.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Document-critique / plan-review model research (context only, no revisions). The reframe from "plan review" to "critical document evaluation" worked, but the payoff was NOT peer review - that seam is nearly empty for model selection (PRISM benchmarks reviewer SYSTEMS on Llama/Qwen backbones, not frontier models). The find is RUBRIC VERIFICATION: RuVerBench arXiv:2606.29920, 2458 human-labelled instances, Cohen kappa 0.808, task is literally ours - given an artifact and a rubric criterion, emit satisfied/not-satisfied. Scored in Balanced Accuracy, so negative recall is half the score and false positives are penalised symmetrically. KEY RESULTS. (1) The 14-position ranking-instability finding REPRODUCES INSIDE ONE PAPER: same metric, same prompt, rankings reorder by up to 5 positions between Deep Research and Agentic Coding domains. (2) Claude Opus 4.7 is the ONLY model that does not move - #3 in both (91.7 / 85.0). (3) Precision finding that outranks the scores: GPT-5.4 tops Agentic Coding BAcc but the paper says it "frequently turn[s] optional or untriggered conditions into requirements" - the exact failure that makes a gate useless. (4) UXBench human evaluation REVERSES its own automated ranking: Claude Sonnet 4.6 first on all 7 human dimensions while Kimi K2.5 drops from #2 automated to #6 human; Gemini-3.1-Pro is #1 on RuVerBench Deep Research and LAST on UXBench. (5) MOST OPERATIONALLY IMPORTANT - Kahneman4Review arXiv:2607.10511 measured judge reliability: cross-VERSION sonnet-3.7 vs sonnet-4-6 gives kappa 0.14 at 33% exact agreement, while cross-VENDOR claude vs gpt-4o gives kappa 0.58. A model version bump changes gate verdicts MORE than swapping vendors. Pin judge model ids and re-baseline on every upgrade. (6) Ticket/issue quality critique: NO head-to-head frontier-model comparison exists; Atlassian benchmarks page 404s; nothing from Linear or GitHub. That domain must be measured in-house. (7) SpecBench arXiv:2605.30314 is the closest task shape but its metric ignores false positives entirely and all per-model numbers are figures - unusable for ranking; useful only as a level-set that nothing exceeds 45% at finding specification deficiencies. (8) Prompt phrasing moves Overall by up to +11.8 points - worth more than model choice at the margin. (9) Fable 5 returns stop_reason "refusal" as HTTP 200, a correctness hazard for an automated gate. RECOMMENDATION from the agent: one model for both roles, Claude Opus 5 with Sonnet 5 as cost tier - chosen on STABILITY across independent streams rather than peak score, with the explicit caveat that Opus 5 has ZERO document-critique coverage and the family-property assumption is exactly what the kappa 0.14 result undermines.
